title: Transitioning from live playback to VOD
lead: Check how the app updates its live display after an event ends, while retaining the same Player and source.

blocks.text: Detecting finalization and updating the display
Each app reads a snapshot that includes duration and updates its live/VOD display state. Check live finalization separately from refreshing the browser or selecting the source again.

The duration-based rule treats a finite, positive duration as VOD and Infinity, zero, or NaN as live. This is an application rule for interpreting SDK snapshots. Apple also records completion for the current live source because an ended HLS source can retain live/infinite SDK getters.

headers: When the state is read again
rows: TimeChanged; also after loading and seek completion

blocks.text: A controlled check without a cloud encoder

A test uses the generated 60-second media and changes the manifest at the same URL to a finalized presentation during playback. Run the first command only if the media has not been generated. Existing output is still never overwritten.
If .cache/test-streams already exists from a successful generation, skip local.py below and start the test with that media. The generator refuses to overwrite an existing output.

python3 encoding/test-streams/local.py
E2E_FINALIZATION_MEDIA_DIR=\
"$PWD/.cache/test-streams/vod-baseline" \
  pnpm --filter @showcase/e2e e2e:finalization

A loopback test server initially advertises real media as live, then finalizes the same manifest URL. HLS uses EXT-X-ENDLIST to indicate that no more segments will be added. DASH changes from a dynamic MPD to a finite static presentation. The suite checks HLS and DASH as separate cases.

The tests exercise Player recreation through the DVR setting, rewind before finalization, finite duration, the VOD display, and seeking afterward. During finalization, they also check that the same Player and source remain active without a new SourceLoaded event. Set E2E_FINALIZATION_PORT if the default port, 5192, is unavailable.

blocks.title: What this test establishes
blocks.text: This is a controlled local finalization check with a real Player and real media. It does not cover production ingest, the encoder, delivery infrastructure, or physical devices.
A finalized VOD can retain its clock origin

Media that used wall-clock time during live playback can retain that origin in its seekable range after becoming finite VOD. In that case, seek(10) is outside the range and is clamped to the start, rather than moving ten seconds into the clip. Add ten to the start of the seekable range instead.

Wait for Seeked before reading relative time to check the completed movement. The app displays relative and absolute time separately. Interpret clock-based displays and latency carefully when the source lacks clock information or the device clock is inaccurate.
Apple HLS completion

On Player 3.128.0, actual HLS completion can leave isLive true and duration infinite. The app records PlaybackFinished only for the current Player and Source that loaded as live, displays ended-live, and disables its live-seek buttons. The shared Live and Sports UIs hide LIVE controls and retain the SDK Replay overlay. Replaying that source keeps its completion state; loading a new source clears it. The SDK timing getters are unchanged.

To read the final manifest as finite VOD, keep the URL and player settings, change only Title under Configure source and playback, and Apply when the action says Reload source. This creates a new Source on the same Player and exact URL; playback position resets. The controlled iOS/tvOS checks require finite duration, a fresh Seeked at 30 seconds and subsequent native playback progress. This manual reload is separate from completion or replay of the original Source.

The Sports UI contains a live-only WallClockLabel and a seek bar, rather than a VOD elapsed-time label. Its custom CSS class needs an explicit hidden rule so the SDK's hide operation removes the live clock outside live playback. The iOS ending check confirms the visible marker halfway through the 60-second clip and hides the live clock. The tvOS hosted check uses the public SDK seek API with visible native video; it does not qualify remote VOD seeking.

On October 21, 2026, the controlled HLS ending checks passed once each on iOS 26.4 and tvOS 26.4 with Player 3.128.0, in 20.875 and 21.362 seconds. They retained the same Player and source through ENDLIST, observed PlaybackFinished, advanced replay, kept app live commands disabled, and checked reset on a new source. Separate Android Player 3.171.0 HLS and DASH cases obtained finite duration and completed VOD seeking on the same source. These are simulator/emulator checks with real media, separate from licensed physical-device behavior.

The extended check passed on October 21, 2026 on iPad / iOS 26.4 in 65.726 seconds and Apple TV / tvOS 26.4 in 65.579 seconds, one test each with zero failures. Both retained live/infinite getters on the completed Source, then reloaded the same URL on the same Player into finite VOD, completed a fresh Seeked at 30 seconds and advanced through native TimeChanged events. The iPad showed the middle seek marker with its live clock hidden; the TV display reached 00:31 / remaining 00:29. These are hosted SDK checks, separate from GUI Apply and remote VOD seeking.

To repeat native checks, use the fixture-server and Finalization scheme commands in the Apple README, or the Android runtime-fixture and PlayerFinalizationInstrumentedTest commands. The native apps require their allowed Player license. tvOS hosted finalization uses SDK start/replay; actual remote Pause/Play is a separate recorded GUI check.
